scope_exclusions: No clinical, public-health, animal, or genome-editing intervention is executed.
No database size, retrospective fit, or protocol design is promoted as a solved-frontier result.
No causal, therapeutic, safety, or generalization claim is earned by this activation packet.

problems.title: Exact Molecular Reaction Dynamics
problems.heuristic_question: Can a reaction-dynamics solver predict an observable it was not tuned on before it asks for scale credit?
problems.current_evidence_boundary: QCArchive now standardizes large quantum-chemistry campaigns and includes reaction energies and nudged-elastic-band profiles, but stored electronic-structure records are not by themselves exact coupled electron-nuclear dynamics.
problems.first_gate: Freeze one low-dimensional reactive scattering model, three incident energies, the potential representation, grid, absorbing boundary, and observable definitions before any candidate output is opened.
problems.denominator: Grid-converged split-operator propagation on the identical potential, grid, time window, and observable extraction code.
problems.primary_metric: Maximum absolute error across preregistered state-to-state reaction probabilities, accompanied by norm-loss and grid-convergence diagnostics.
problems.acceptance_rule: All three unopened energies must have probability error <= 1e-3, norm-accounting error <= 1e-8, and a documented cost comparison against the same-access denominator.
problems.falsifier: Any unopened energy violates the probability or norm threshold, or the result depends on a changed grid, potential, time window, or observable extractor.
problems.data_split: One disclosed pilot energy for debugging; three unopened energies for acceptance.
problems.safety_boundary: Computational chemistry only; no wet-lab reaction recommendation or materials-safety claim.
problems.next_artifact: P049 frozen model specification plus an independently replayable split-operator denominator transcript.

source.title: QCArchive record and computation types
source.latest_update: Current documentation includes reaction-energy and NEB reaction-profile records.

problems.title: Programmable Self-Assembling Matter
problems.heuristic_question: If off-target interactions are part of the physics, can inverse design still win on structures it never saw?
problems.current_evidence_boundary: A 2026 DNA-origami study reports that scaffold sequences with fewer predicted off-target interactions fold more reliably across several 2D and 3D targets, making unseen-defect robustness a concrete denominator rather than a qualitative aspiration.
problems.first_gate: Freeze a library of target structures, an assembly simulator, a design-call budget, and a hidden panel of off-target binding and component-dropout conditions.
problems.denominator: Budget-matched random search and a target-only inverse-design baseline that does not model off-target interactions.
problems.primary_metric: Assembly yield on hidden defect conditions, with off-target structure rate reported separately.
problems.acceptance_rule: The preregistered design must improve median hidden-condition yield by at least 10 percentage points over both denominators without increasing the off-target structure rate.
problems.falsifier: The gain disappears on hidden defect conditions, requires more design calls, or trades yield for an increased off-target rate.
problems.data_split: Disclosed target topologies for development; held-out target topology and defect panel for acceptance.
problems.safety_boundary: In-silico assembly only; no biological delivery, environmental release, or autonomous active-matter experiment.
problems.next_artifact: P050 simulator contract with seeded target/defect splits and budget-matched baseline implementations.

source.title: Optimising DNA origami assembly by reducing off-target interactions
source.latest_update: Published 2026-05-26; experimentally links predicted off-target reactions to folding yield.

problems.title: Protein Dynamics and Function Prediction
problems.heuristic_question: Can an ensemble prediction explain held-out dynamics that a beautiful single structure cannot?
problems.current_evidence_boundary: AlphaFold DB expanded high-confidence complex predictions in 2026, while its own FAQ states that a prediction is not a Boltzmann sample and that known multiple conformations usually collapse to one output.
problems.first_gate: Select proteins with paired structural models and experimental dynamic observables; freeze observable preprocessing and exclude the acceptance observables from ensemble fitting.
problems.denominator: Best available single-structure prediction plus a short conventional molecular-dynamics ensemble under the same experimental restraints.
problems.primary_metric: Normalized error on held-out NMR or conformational-population observables, stratified by protein and observable type.
problems.acceptance_rule: The candidate ensemble must reduce median held-out normalized error by at least 20% versus both denominators and retain the gain under leave-one-protein-out replay.
problems.falsifier: The gain is confined to fitted restraints, vanishes under leave-one-protein-out replay, or is explained by a larger sampling budget.
problems.data_split: Restraint-level holdout within proteins plus a protein-level holdout.
problems.safety_boundary: Public structural and biophysical data only; no clinical interpretation or protein-engineering safety claim.
problems.next_artifact: P051 small benchmark roster with explicit experimental observables, licensing, and single-structure/MD denominators.

source.title: AlphaFold Protein Structure Database FAQ
source.latest_update: May 2026 database release added large complex-prediction sets while retaining explicit ensemble limitations.

problems.title: Genotype-to-Phenotype Mapping
problems.heuristic_question: Does a genotype-to-phenotype model survive a change of ancestry, environment, and measurement protocol?
problems.current_evidence_boundary: The NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog exposes harmonized summary statistics, ancestry metadata, and, from April 2026, standards for CNV and gene-based results; association resources still do not turn correlation into a general causal map.
problems.first_gate: Freeze one quantitative trait, harmonized studies from at least two ancestry groups, covariates, and a cohort-level external holdout before model selection.
problems.denominator: An additive polygenic-score model using the same variants, summary statistics, covariates, and training cohorts.
problems.primary_metric: External-cohort calibration slope and incremental explained variance over the additive denominator, reported by ancestry group.
problems.acceptance_rule: Every held-out ancestry group must have calibration slope in [0.9, 1.1] and positive incremental explained variance with a bootstrap interval excluding zero.
problems.falsifier: Any ancestry group fails calibration, the incremental interval includes zero, or hidden cohort information enters harmonization or feature selection.
problems.data_split: Study-level and ancestry-level holdout; no random row split across related samples or cohorts.
problems.safety_boundary: Summary statistics only; no re-identification, individual prediction, reproductive selection, or clinical decision use.
problems.next_artifact: P052 trait-specific accession manifest and ancestry-aware leakage audit.

source.title: GWAS Catalog summary statistics documentation
source.latest_update: April 2026 standards extend beyond SNP-only submissions and preserve ancestry/sample metadata.

problems.title: General Early Cancer Detection and Personalized Cure
problems.heuristic_question: What evidence would distinguish an early-cancer signal from an expensive cascade of false positives?
problems.current_evidence_boundary: NCI's active Vanguard Study randomizes up to 24,000 cancer-free adults among two multi-cancer detection tests and a control arm to establish feasibility before a definitive mortality trial.
problems.first_gate: Adopt a prospective population-screening protocol that freezes eligibility, assay threshold, diagnostic-resolution pathway, cancer ascertainment, and follow-up before outcomes are opened.
problems.denominator: Standard-of-care screening in a randomized control arm, not a retrospective case-control sample.
problems.primary_metric: Cancer-specific positive predictive value and diagnostic-resolution burden, with stage distribution and false-negative cancers reported.
problems.acceptance_rule: No promotable detection claim until a prospective randomized study meets its preregistered predictive-value and diagnostic-burden thresholds; no cure claim without treatment-specific randomized outcomes.
problems.falsifier: Performance falls below the preregistered prospective thresholds, downstream diagnostic harm is excessive, or retrospective tuning enters the evaluation set.
problems.data_split: Prospective randomized arms and locked analysis plan; retrospective samples may be pilot-only.
problems.safety_boundary: No medical advice, assay recommendation, patient recruitment, treatment selection, or cure claim.
problems.next_artifact: P053 endpoint dictionary that separates detection feasibility, mortality benefit, and personalized-treatment evidence.

source.title: The Vanguard Study on Multi-Cancer Detection Tests

problems.title: Mechanisms and Safe Reversal of Aging
problems.heuristic_question: If lifespan moves, what would prove that function improved without merely changing how disease was counted?
problems.current_evidence_boundary: NIA's Interventions Testing Program runs standardized studies at three sites in genetically heterogeneous mice, uses pilot toxicity testing, and expands promising agents to health, pathology, and mechanism endpoints.
problems.first_gate: Use a blinded, multi-site, sex-stratified protocol with frozen dosing, pilot toxicity, survival, function, pathology, and tumor endpoints.
problems.denominator: Concurrent vehicle control under the same husbandry and a three-site protocol modeled on the NIA ITP.
problems.primary_metric: Site-pooled survival effect paired with prespecified late-life function and pathology outcomes.
problems.acceptance_rule: A candidate advances only if survival and at least one late-life functional endpoint improve, direction is not reversed at any site, and tumor/pathology safety guardrails do not worsen.
problems.falsifier: The survival effect is site-specific, functional outcomes do not improve, or any preregistered toxicity or tumor guardrail worsens.
problems.data_split: Pilot toxicity stage followed by independent multi-site efficacy stage; both sexes reported separately.
problems.safety_boundary: No animal experiment is executed here; no human anti-aging recommendation or extrapolation.
problems.next_artifact: P054 endpoint and adverse-event ontology aligned to public ITP outcomes.

source.title: Interventions Testing Program
source.latest_update: Updated 2026-05-12; documents three-site SOPs, pilot toxicity, and staged efficacy testing.

problems.title: Neurodegenerative Disease Root Causes
problems.heuristic_question: Can a proposed mechanism predict who changes next, not merely describe who is already ill?
problems.current_evidence_boundary: ADNI provides longitudinal, multi-center observational data and aggregate views from more than 2,500 participants to validate biomarkers for Alzheimer's disease trials.
problems.first_gate: Freeze one mechanism-derived biomarker signature, a future clinical-change window, site-aware preprocessing, and an untouched acquisition-site holdout.
problems.denominator: Age, sex, APOE status, baseline diagnosis, and baseline cognition without the proposed mechanism-derived features.
problems.primary_metric: Calibration and time-dependent prediction error for prospective cognitive or diagnostic change on the site holdout.
problems.acceptance_rule: The mechanism signature must improve held-out prediction error with a bootstrap interval excluding zero and remain calibrated across site and sex strata.
problems.falsifier: No incremental predictive value remains, calibration fails in a prespecified stratum, or the signature uses post-baseline information.
problems.data_split: Participant-, family-, time-, and acquisition-site-separated holdout.
problems.safety_boundary: Observational biomarker research only; prediction does not establish a root cause or treatment effect.
problems.next_artifact: P055 ADNI variable/timepoint manifest and post-baseline leakage sentinel.

source.title: ADNI data portal
source.latest_update: Current portal reports a longitudinal multi-center cohort with more than 2,500 participants.

problems.title: Programmable Immune Control
problems.heuristic_question: Can an immune controller hit its target state without borrowing success from cytokine toxicity?
problems.current_evidence_boundary: ImmPort exposes standardized clinical-trial, flow-cytometry, gene-expression, intervention, and adverse-event data, enabling donor-held-out retrospective control tests but not safe prospective immune programming.
problems.first_gate: Select a perturbation study with matched baseline, response, dose, and adverse-event measurements; freeze target and guardrail biomarkers before model fitting.
problems.denominator: No-treatment or standard-treatment arm plus a linear dose-response model using the same donor information.
problems.primary_metric: Held-out donor target-state error with separate cytokine, off-target-cell-state, and adverse-event guardrails.
problems.acceptance_rule: Target-state error must improve versus both denominators while every prespecified guardrail is non-inferior on donor-held-out data.
problems.falsifier: Apparent control requires donor leakage, a guardrail worsens, or benefit is confined to one study batch.
problems.data_split: Donor- and study-level holdouts; no cell-level random split across the same donor.
problems.safety_boundary: Retrospective public-data analysis only; no dosing, immunotherapy, or clinical control recommendation.
problems.next_artifact: P056 ImmPort study shortlist with donor-key, intervention, assay, and adverse-event completeness checks.

source.title: ImmPort Documentation
source.latest_update: Current repository supports immunology, clinical-trial, flow-cytometry, gene-expression, intervention, and adverse-event data.
source.access: free registration; controlled data may require approval

problems.title: Global Reversal of Antimicrobial Resistance
problems.heuristic_question: Can an AMR forecast beat yesterday's resistance rate where surveillance is thinnest?
problems.current_evidence_boundary: WHO GLASS standardizes resistance and antimicrobial-use surveillance and its 2025 global report provides a current cross-country evidence base; surveillance coverage and comparability remain part of the problem.
problems.first_gate: Freeze one pathogen-drug pair, country-year eligibility rules, missingness policy, and future-year holdout before forecasting.
problems.denominator: Last-observation-carried-forward and a country-specific logistic time trend using the same GLASS rows.
problems.primary_metric: Calibration and weighted absolute error for held-out resistance prevalence, stratified by surveillance completeness.
problems.acceptance_rule: The candidate must beat both denominators overall and in the lowest-completeness prespecified stratum without excluding countries after outcomes are seen.
problems.falsifier: The gain disappears in sparse-surveillance settings, calibration fails, or post-outcome completeness filtering changes the cohort.
problems.data_split: Forward-chaining country-year holdout with country-level robustness replay.
problems.safety_boundary: Population-level surveillance analysis only; no antibiotic prescribing or pathogen-engineering guidance.
problems.next_artifact: P057 pathogen-drug-country coverage matrix and missing-not-at-random sensitivity plan.

source.title: Global Antimicrobial Resistance and Use Surveillance System
source.latest_update: GLASS lists the Global antibiotic resistance surveillance report 2025.

problems.title: Pandemic Prediction and Interdiction
problems.heuristic_question: How early is an early warning after false alarms and reporting delays are charged to the score?
problems.current_evidence_boundary: CDC's 2026 wastewater program covers multiple viruses, updates public dashboards weekly, and describes wastewater as an early-warning signal that must be interpreted with clinical surveillance.
problems.first_gate: Freeze jurisdictions, pathogens, reporting-delay simulation, alert thresholds, and a future seasonal window before producing alerts.
problems.denominator: Seasonal historical average, last-value trend, and clinical-data-only alerting at the same false-alert budget.
problems.primary_metric: Median lead time before a clinical threshold, conditional on a prespecified false-alert rate and data-availability lag.
problems.acceptance_rule: Wastewater-plus-clinical alerting must gain at least seven median days over every denominator while staying within the frozen false-alert budget on unseen jurisdictions and weeks.
problems.falsifier: Lead time is below seven days, false alerts exceed budget, or the gain vanishes after realistic reporting delays.
problems.data_split: Geographic and forward-time holdout with vintage-aware data snapshots.
problems.safety_boundary: Retrospective forecasting only; no live public-health alert or interdiction action.
problems.next_artifact: P058 vintage-aware CDC data manifest and alert-score replay harness.

source.publisher: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
source.title: About Wastewater Data
source.latest_update: Updated 2026-04-10; documents multi-virus weekly data, early warning, and clinical-data complementarity.

problems.title: Human Brain Connectome and Cognition
problems.heuristic_question: Can a connectome predict cognition after family structure, head motion, and scanner artifacts are denied an escape route?
problems.current_evidence_boundary: The HCP-Young Adult 2025 release provides updated processed imaging for 1,071 subjects and phenotypic data for 1,206, with documented processing changes and quality-control exclusions.
problems.first_gate: Freeze one cognitive endpoint, motion and acquisition covariates, family groups, connectome construction, and an untouched family-level holdout.
problems.denominator: Demographics, motion, scanner/acquisition variables, and regional anatomy without functional-connectivity edges.
problems.primary_metric: Family-held-out prediction error and test-retest reliability, with incremental value over the full nuisance denominator.
problems.acceptance_rule: Connectivity must add reproducible held-out value with a bootstrap interval excluding zero and no material degradation after motion-matched replay.
problems.falsifier: The increment disappears after family-aware or motion-matched replay, or test-retest reliability is below the preregistered floor.
problems.data_split: Family-separated train/validation/test split; retest participants used only for reliability.
problems.safety_boundary: Research-only neuroimaging; no individual cognitive diagnosis, identity inference, or causal cognition claim.
problems.next_artifact: P059 HCP-YA 2025 subject-family/QC manifest and nuisance-only denominator.

source.title: HCP Young Adult
source.latest_update: 2025 release lists 1,071 processed imaging subjects and phenotypic data for 1,206 subjects.

problems.title: Safe Scalable Gene Editing
problems.heuristic_question: What would make an editing result fail even when its on-target number looks excellent?
problems.current_evidence_boundary: FDA's 2024 final genome-editing guidance covers design, manufacturing, nonclinical safety, and trials; 2026 draft guidances separately address next-generation-sequencing safety assessment and reuse of prior knowledge.
problems.first_gate: Freeze one somatic-cell edit, manufacturing lot criteria, on-target assay, orthogonal off-target assays, chromosomal-integrity tests, and long-term follow-up triggers.
problems.denominator: Unedited cells, mock delivery, and the current standard editor/delivery system assessed with identical assays and sequencing depth.
problems.primary_metric: On-target functional correction reported jointly with off-target edits, structural variants, chromosomal integrity, viability, immunogenicity, and lot variability.
problems.acceptance_rule: No safety or scalability claim is promotable unless every assay-specific threshold is preregistered, met across independent lots, and non-inferior to the standard editor at matched sequencing sensitivity.
problems.falsifier: Any safety threshold fails, a signal is assay-specific and not orthogonally confirmed, or scale changes lot variability or detection sensitivity.
problems.data_split: Independent manufacturing lots and blinded assay laboratories; discovery and confirmation assays remain separate.
problems.safety_boundary: No sequence design, wet-lab editing, germline work, clinical recommendation, or claim of FDA compliance.
problems.next_artifact: P060 assay-and-lot evidence matrix aligned to final and draft FDA guidance.

source.title: Cellular & Gene Therapy Guidances
source.latest_update: April-June 2026 draft guidances add NGS safety assessment and prior-knowledge considerations to the 2024 final guidance.
